title: Background system
purpose: Describes what sits behind the subject, how much and how it moves, how it changes per beat and how it could be generated procedurally.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F5 on the border bands (top 15%, bottom 15%, side 10%) for motion; F1 frames per beat; F6 for luminance.
pitfalls: Measuring background motion in a region covered by text or the subject
Calling a slow zoom on a photo a moving background
Ignoring compression noise when the motion level is near zero

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F2: Burst sheet, 10 frames over 1 s: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 1 -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=10,scale=270:-2,tile=5x2" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/burst_T.jpg"
recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F5: Per-frame motion in a region (mean absolute frame difference, 0-255): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "crop=iw:ih*0.15:0:0,tblend=all_mode=difference,signalstats,metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=$WORK/diff.txt" -an -f null -  (drop the crop for the full frame)
recipes.F6: Per-frame colour statistics (YMIN, YAVG, YMAX, SATAVG, HUEMED, UAVG, VAVG): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -vf "signalstats,metadata=mode=print:file=$WORK/stats.txt" -an -f null -
recipes.F9: Average colour of a region: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y,scale=1:1:flags=area,format=rgb24" -f rawvideo - | od -An -tu1
recipes.F10: Similarity of two frames (SSIM, 1.0 = identical): ffmpeg -i a.jpg -i b.jpg -lavfi "[0:v]scale=320:-2[a];[1:v]scale=320:-2[b];[a][b]ssim" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o "All:[0-9.]*"
recipes.F12: Black frames: ffmpeg -i "$SRC" -vf "blackdetect=d=0.05:pix_th=0.10" -an -f null - 2>&1 | grep black_

questions.question: What is the background made of (looping video, still image, gradient, procedural pattern, blurred copy of the foreground, solid colour)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the bottom layer kind.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect border regions on F1 frames across beats and F2 bursts; a blurred copy mirrors foreground colours and shapes.
questions.challenge: Compare background regions with the foreground at the same time (F10 on downscaled crops) before calling it a blurred copy.

questions.question: Does the background move during every shot?
questions.why_it_matters: Checks the moving-background rule.
questions.how_to_answer: F5 on the top 15% and bottom 15% bands (regions without text); a shot passes when the mean difference exceeds 0.6 (0-255 scale, the threshold the short_video_house_style rules use) for every 2 s window. Also read evidence.shots[].motion_energy.border.
questions.challenge: Make sure the measured band contains no text, subject or camera zoom; a zoom on a photo moves the band too.

questions.question: What is the background motion level (mean absolute frame difference in background regions, median over shots)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills background_motion_level as a measurable number.
questions.how_to_answer: Median over shots of evidence.shots[].motion_energy.border (video_re_motion_energy: mean absolute grey-level difference between consecutive frames, 0-255, at 160 px analysis width, outside the central 60% x 60% box). Cross-check 3 shots with F5 on text-free bands.
questions.challenge: The border region includes captions and titles that animate; compare with F5 on a text-free band and report both.

questions.question: Does the background change per beat, per shot, or stay the same for the whole video?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes the background_per_beat parameter.
questions.how_to_answer: F10 SSIM between background crops at the start of each beat.
questions.challenge: A looping video gives different frames over time; compare the same loop phase or judge by content.

questions.question: What are the background's dominant colours?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds background colours to the palette.
questions.how_to_answer: F9 average colour of background crops in 5 shots, or evidence.shots[].palette when the background dominates the frame.
questions.challenge: Palettes from whole frames include the photo; use background-only crops.

questions.question: How much darker or lighter is the background than the foreground subject (luma difference)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a separation rule.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 YAVG on a background crop versus a subject crop in 5 shots.
questions.challenge: Report all 5 pairs; one bright shot can dominate a mean.

questions.question: How blurred is the background (sharp, soft, heavy blur)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets background blur strength.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 enlarged crops of the background; heavy blur shows no edges finer than about 2% of frame width.
questions.challenge: Compare with a known sharp edge in the same frame.

questions.question: Is there a repeating grid, dot or line pattern, and what is its spacing in px?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a grid layer with spacing.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crop of the background; measure distance between repeated lines.
questions.challenge: Report spacing and line width; check that it is not a compression artefact.

questions.question: Does the background loop, and what is the loop period in seconds?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the loop length for a background asset.
questions.how_to_answer: F10 SSIM between a background crop at time t and later times; the first time with SSIM above 0.95 (excluding t+0) gives the period.
questions.challenge: Foreground elements change the crop; use a band with background only.

questions.question: Which way does the background move (drift up, down, sideways, radial, rotating, turbulent)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the background motion direction.
questions.how_to_answer: Track a background feature over F2 bursts.
questions.challenge: Track at least two features; say if they disagree.

questions.question: How many sub-layers make up the background (for example gradient plus texture plus particles plus light)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets background layer depth.
questions.how_to_answer: Separate elements by different motion or blend behaviour on F2 bursts.
questions.challenge: Require one observable cue per sub-layer.

questions.question: Does the background react to the audio (pulses or flashes on beats or onsets)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds an audio-reactive rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Correlate F5 background-band differences or F6 YAVG per frame with evidence.audio.onsets_s; check peaks within 80 ms of onsets.
questions.challenge: Compare against random time shifts; reaction must beat chance clearly.

questions.question: Does the background hue shift over time, and how fast (degrees per second)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a hue-cycle parameter.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 HUEMED on background-only crops sampled every 2 s.
questions.challenge: Shot changes cause jumps; measure within long shots.

questions.question: Is the background less saturated than the foreground, and by how much (SATAVG ratio)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a saturation separation rule.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 SATAVG on background versus subject crops.
questions.challenge: Report all measured pairs.

questions.question: Is the background thematically tied to the topic (for example water for an ocean topic) or generic?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes the background_theme parameter (asset search hint or generic default).
questions.how_to_answer: Compare background content with the item subjects on F1 frames.
questions.challenge: Method must be observed; one themed shot does not make the system themed.

questions.question: What share of the frame shows background (not covered by the main visual or text)?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the generator how visible the background is.
questions.how_to_answer: 1 - main visual coverage - text area, measured on F1 frames in 5 shots.
questions.challenge: Semi-transparent foreground layers still let background show; say how they were counted.

questions.question: Is the background derived from the foreground image (a zoomed, blurred copy)?
questions.why_it_matters: Selects a cheap, always-matching background method.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare colours and large shapes of the background with the foreground image at the same time.
questions.challenge: When the foreground changes, a derived background must change at the same frame.

questions.question: Are there light sweeps or rays crossing the background, and how often?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a light-sweep sub-layer with period.
questions.how_to_answer: F2 bursts and F6 YAVG series on background bands; periodic bright passes indicate sweeps.
questions.challenge: Give the period from at least two passes.

questions.question: How fast does background content drift, in px per second at full resolution?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the background speed parameter.
questions.how_to_answer: Track a feature across F1 frames 1 s apart.
questions.challenge: Track two features; report both.

questions.question: Does the background brightness pulse or flicker, and with what amplitude?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a pulse parameter or confirms a steady background.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 YAVG per frame on a background band; report peak-to-peak range within shots.
questions.challenge: Exclude frames at cuts.

questions.question: Do background changes line up with item beat boundaries?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a sync rule between structure and background.
questions.how_to_answer: Background change times (from 004) compared with beat starts; share within 0.3 s.
questions.challenge: If the background never changes, answer not applicable in the note and ratio 0 with low confidence.

questions.question: What procedural recipe would reproduce the background (for example gradient plus noise plus drifting particles), expressed as ffmpeg filters or a renderer recipe?
questions.why_it_matters: Lets new videos generate the background without sourcing footage.
questions.how_to_answer: From 001, 008, 010, 013 and 019, write a recipe using real ffmpeg sources and filters (for example gradients, noise, geq, hue, scroll) or the project's renderer, with measured parameters.
questions.challenge: Every filter named must exist in ffmpeg (check with ffmpeg -filters); render 2 s and compare motion level with 003.

questions.question: What background parameters should a new video set (kind, asset or recipe, speed, colours, per-beat change)?
questions.why_it_matters: Feeds the parameteriser.
questions.how_to_answer: Collect 001, 003, 004, 005 and 019 into typed parameters with ranges from the observed spread.
questions.challenge: Each parameter must cite derived_from.

questions.question: Is the background kept calm behind text (less detail or motion where captions and titles sit)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a legibility rule for background placement.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare edge density and F5 motion in the caption band against other bands.
questions.challenge: A frosted panel already calms the area; say whether the background itself is calmer.

questions.question: How busy is the background directly behind the captions (edge density or local contrast)?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives a measurable busyness limit for caption areas.
questions.how_to_answer: On F3 crops of the caption band without text, run ffmpeg -vf edgedetect,signalstats and read YAVG: YAVG / 255 approximates the share of edge pixels. Report crop coordinates and the value.
questions.challenge: Report crop coordinates so the measurement can be repeated.

questions.question: Are there depth cues inside the background (bokeh circles, haze, perspective lines)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds depth elements to the background recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect F3 background crops.
questions.challenge: Name the timestamp for each cue.

questions.question: Is the background in the hook different from the body background?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a hook-specific background option.
questions.how_to_answer: F10 SSIM and F9 colour comparison between hook and first item background crops.
questions.challenge: Compare against variation between two body items; the hook difference must exceed it.

questions.question: Is the background footage vertical-native or cropped from horizontal footage?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the asset step which footage orientation to source.
questions.how_to_answer: Look for cropped subjects at the sides, upscaling softness (F3), and composition centred for 16:9.
questions.challenge: Mark as inferred unless an edge cut-off is visible.

questions.question: What is the temporal character of background motion: slow drift (under one cycle per 5 s), moderate, or busy (several changes per second)?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives a qualitative speed class tied to a number.
questions.how_to_answer: Use 003 and 019; classify with the stated boundaries and report the numbers.
questions.challenge: The class must be consistent with the measured values.

questions.question: Does the background motion level stay steady or spike at transitions?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a rule for transition energy versus steady motion.
questions.how_to_answer: Plot F5 border-band means over time (list values per second); compare values within 0.5 s of cuts to the rest.
questions.challenge: Cuts themselves create a one-frame spike in F5; exclude the cut frame.

questions.question: What is the background's luminance range across shots (YAVG min and max)?
questions.why_it_matters: Bounds background brightness in the grade.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 YAVG on background bands per shot; report min, median and max.
questions.challenge: Report which shots were measured.

questions.question: Does the background ever drop to plain black or white (dips), and for how long?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds dips as transition devices or rules them out.
questions.how_to_answer: F12 blackdetect for black; F6 YMIN above 235 across a frame for white.
questions.challenge: Fade-ins at the start and end are separate from mid-video dips.
